deep.reconstruction:
Context: the page belongs to a calculation of the elastic Green's function (point-force solution) for a slab -a/2<x<a/2, and presumably for a rectangular box, by the method of images. The next page sums lattices of images (xi+2ma, eta+2nb, zeta+2pc), uses (-1)^{m+n+p} and theta-function or Fourier transformations, and writes the base solution as u=(lam+mu) d^2phi/dx^2 - 2(lam+2mu)/rho with phi=rho. The Lamé constants are lam, mu. N_i are normal stresses and T_i shear stresses (T_1=tau_yz, T_2=tau_zx, T_3=tau_xy). Throughout, the transcription's '∫' signs before (x-xi) or before derivatives are, in my judgment, Riemann's bracket strokes and not integrals. The exception is the explicit '∫...∂y' in the image-correction terms, which is a genuine integral in y.

(1) Base solution, a point force in the x-direction at (xi,eta,zeta), with rho = distance:
u=(lam+mu)(x-xi) d(1/rho)/dx + (lam+mu)/rho - 2(lam+2mu)/rho
v=(lam+mu)(x-xi) d(1/rho)/dy
w=(lam+mu)(x-xi) d(1/rho)/dz
Since d^2 rho/dx dx_j = delta_{xj}/rho + (x-xi) d_j(1/rho), this is u_j=(lam+mu) d_x d_j rho - 2(lam+2mu) delta_{xj}/rho. Up to sign and normalisation, u_x ~ (lam+3mu)/rho + (lam+mu)(x-xi)^2/rho^3, which is Kelvin's 1848 solution.

(2) Dilatation: theta = 2(lam+mu) d_x(1/rho) - 2(lam+2mu) d_x(1/rho) = -2mu d_x(1/rho). [Implicit, mine: then mu*Lap u + (lam+mu) grad theta = 0 away from the source, because Lap[(x-xi)f] = 2 f_x for harmonic f.]

(3) Stresses of the base solution:
N2/mu = lam theta/mu + 2 v_y = -2lam d_x(1/rho) + 2(lam+mu)(x-xi) d_yy(1/rho)
T3/mu = u_y + v_x = 2(lam+mu)(x-xi) d_xy(1/rho) + [2(lam+mu) - 2(lam+2mu)] d_y(1/rho)
T1/mu = 2(lam+mu)(x-xi) d_yz(1/rho)

(4) Treating the faces y = const. Riemann applies an operator to N2, '(1/mu)(y ∫^y Lap^2 N2 dy + (x,z)) - 2N2'. Its result is 4(lam+mu) y d_xy(1/rho) + 4lam d_x(1/rho) - 4(lam+mu)(x-xi) d_yy(1/rho). He gives the companion shear stresses:
T3 = 4(lam+mu) y d_yy - 4(lam+mu)(x-xi) d_xy - 2(lam+mu) d_y + 4(lam+2mu) d_y
T1 = 4(lam+mu) y d_yz - 4(lam+mu)(x-xi) d_yz
These read as the residual tractions to be cancelled after reflecting the source in a face y = const. The note 'y-2nb' marks the images at eta+2nb.

The corrections attached to the n-th image are (displacement assignment best read with the next page):
u = nb·2(lam+mu) ∫ d_xx(1/rho) dy
v = nb·2(lam+mu) d_x(1/rho)
w = nb·2(lam+mu) ∫ d_xz(1/rho) dy
with N2/mu = nb·4(lam+mu) d_xy(1/rho). This is a displacement c·grad psi with psi = ∫ d_x(1/rho) dy harmonic and c = 2(lam+mu)nb. Hence theta = 0 and N2 = 2 mu c psi_yy.

(5) Right half: the same for the faces x = ±a/2.
u = 2(lam+mu) x d_xx(1/rho) + (lam+mu)/rho + (lam+2mu)(...) — partly illegible
v = (lam+mu) x d_xy + (lam+2mu) y d_x
w = ...
The residual tractions are:
'(1/mu)(x ∫^x Lap^2 N1 dx + (y,z)) - 2N1 = (lam+mu) xi d_xx + 4(lam+2mu) d_x'
T3 = 4(lam+mu) xi d_xy + 4mu d_y
T2 = 4(lam+mu) xi d_xz + 4mu d_z
Here the correct coefficient -2mu of the base T3 is used, so 4mu = -2·(-2mu).

(6) Image bookkeeping: successive reflections of xi in x = ±a/2 give -a-xi, -xi, xi, a-xi, 2a+xi, ... In general these are xi + (even)a and (odd)a - xi, i.e. xi+2ma and (2m+1)a-xi, as on the next page.

(7) Final slab form:
N1/mu = -2lam d_x(1/rho) + 2(lam+mu)(...)d_xxx - 4(lam+2mu)(...)d_x + na·4(lam+mu) d_xx(1/rho_n)
T3/mu = ... + na·4(lam+mu) d_xy
T2/mu = ... + na·4(lam+mu) d_xz
(u,v,w) = ... + na·2(lam+mu) grad(1/rho_n)
That is, each image carries an added harmonic-gradient displacement 2(lam+mu)·na·grad(1/rho_n), whose stresses are 2 mu times the Hessian. This is internally consistent: N1 = 2mu c h_xx and T3 = 2mu c h_xy with c = 2(lam+mu)na.

Purpose: build the Green's tensor of the elastic slab or box from Kelvin's solution, using images plus correction fields proportional to the image offset. On the next page the image lattice sums are converted to Fourier/theta series.
errors: T3/mu for the base solution: the page has (lam+mu) d_y(1/rho) - 2(lam+2mu) d_y(1/rho). The correct value from u_y+v_x is 2(lam+mu) d_y - 2(lam+2mu) d_y = -2mu d_y(1/rho); one (lam+mu) term is dropped.
The T3 slip propagates into the left-hand residual T3 = ... -2(lam+mu) d_y + 4(lam+2mu) d_y. The right-hand computation uses the correct 4mu d_y, so Riemann evidently corrected it there.

The meaning and exact form of the operator '(1/mu)(y ∫^y Lap^2 N2 dy + (x,z)) - 2N2' cannot be verified from the page. The right-hand side '(lam+mu) xi d_xx + 4(lam+2mu) d_x' for the x-faces is not obviously the analogue of the y-face formula (one would expect a factor 4(lam+mu) and terms analogous to 4lam d_x); possible slip or misreading.

The corrections grow linearly in n (na, nb). Convergence of the image series is not addressed on this page; it is handled only implicitly on the next page via alternating signs and theta transformation.

results.what: Point-force (Kelvin) solution in the form u_j=(lam+mu) d_x d_j rho - 2(lam+2mu) delta_xj/rho, with dilatation -2mu d_x(1/rho)
results.modern_name: Kelvin solution / elastic Green's tensor (Galerkin-vector form)

results.what: Stress components N2, T3, T1 of the Kelvin solution

Method of images for a slab or box with extra correction fields proportional to the image offset, notably harmonic-gradient displacements 2(lam+mu)·na·grad(1/rho_n), to cancel residual tractions on the faces
results.modern_name: Image method for elastic half-space/slab Green's function (cf. Mindlin's 1936 half-space solution with offset-proportional image terms)
results.usually_credited_to: Mindlin 1936 (half-space); slab and box problems Lamé 1852 onward, image treatments much later

results.what: Image positions xi+2ma and (2m+1)a-xi for the slab |x|<a/2
results.modern_name: Reflection group of a slab (periodic images)

deep.surprise_reason: The Kelvin-solution algebra is routine. What is notable is an unpublished attempt at the elastic Green's tensor of a slab or box via images with offset-proportional harmonic correction terms, reminiscent of Mindlin (1936). Combined with the next page's theta-function summation, this is a substantive unpublished research fragment, but it is incomplete, partly erroneous, and not clearly a finished result.

checkable.sympy: x,y,z,xi,lam,mu=symbols('x y z xi lam mu'); r=sqrt((x-xi)**2+y**2+z**2); u=(lam+mu)*(x-xi)*diff(1/r,x)+(lam+mu)/r-2*(lam+2*mu)/r; v=(lam+mu)*(x-xi)*diff(1/r,y); w=(lam+mu)*(x-xi)*diff(1/r,z); th=diff(u,x)+diff(v,y)+diff(w,z); simplify(th+2*mu*diff(1/r,x))

checkable.asserts: the base displacement satisfies Navier's equations away from the source (all 0)
N2/mu formula on the page is correct (0)
correct T3/mu has coefficient -2mu on d_y(1/rho) (0); Riemann's version with a single (lam+mu) is off by (lam+mu)*d_y(1/rho)
harmonic-gradient correction has zero dilatation, N1=2mu c h_xx, T3=2mu c h_xy, matching the na*4(lam+mu) stress terms for c=2(lam+mu)na

checkable.sympy: a,s=symbols('a s'); R1=lambda t: a-t; R2=lambda t: -a-t; [simplify(R1(s)-(a-s)), simplify(R2(R1(s))-(s-2*a)), simplify(R1(R2(s))-(2*a+s))]
checkable.asserts: reflections in x=±a/2 generate images xi+2ma and (2m+1)a-xi

transcription_corrections: The '∫' signs before (x-xi) and before single derivatives, e.g. 'u=(lam+mu)∫(x-xi)d(1/rho)/dx', are probably bracket strokes and not integrals; the formulas check only if read without integration.

In the lower-left block (corrections with nb), the displacement labels appear scrambled. Consistent with the next page, they should read u = nb·2(lam+mu)∫ d_xx(1/rho) dy, v = nb·2(lam+mu) d_x(1/rho), w = nb·2(lam+mu)∫ d_xz(1/rho) dy (the first line begins with a struck/overwritten 'v').
'y - 2nb' is an image-position note (images at eta+2nb), not an equation fragment.
Image list should read: -a-xi, -xi, xi, a-xi, 2a+xi; the marginal '(m+1)a-xi' is the generic odd reflection (2m+1)a-xi.
